summary: Test-writing run for #39. The client/server solver contract is now enforced: the upstream golden-vector corpus (viamin/color_matching priv/parity/v1/corpus.json) is committed as a fixture and replayed through WeightedSquaredErrorScorer and the real CompositionSolver path, asserting every score, exclusion, selection, error and tie index exactly (7 tests, green). A second contract test pins the published OpenAPI document to the two /api/v1 endpoints and response shapes the app decodes; it fails on purpose until the document is vendored for the generated client (6 red tests, expected in this phase). The existing disk-cache suite is unchanged and green (69 tests). README and docs/solver-parity-corpus.md record where the corpus lives, how to refresh it and the parity findings. The generated client, its migration and the PR body remain implementation-phase work. Verification ran with Swift 6.4.2 on Linux over the portable Foundation subset of the package (the two Apple-only files BrightnessGridSampler.swift / BrightnessColorSpaceTests.swift and the pre-existing PaletteAPIClientTests.swift Swift-6.4 compile error were excluded; bin/lint's Linux harness fails the same way on the base commit 95437fe, so that breakage is pre-existing and unrelated).

references.result: red_by_design: 6 tests fail with 'No vendored OpenAPI document was found' until the OpenAPI document is committed for swift-openapi-generator; verified locally with Swift 6.4.2 on Linux

acceptance_criteria.reason: Adding swift-openapi-generator/swift-openapi-runtime, vendoring the document and migrating PaletteAPIClient are implementation changes, which this test-writing run must not make. The contract test written here gates them and fails loudly until the document is committed.
